title: Rebuke by word and chastisement by wrath
english: "Lord, do not rebuke me in your fury" (Psalm 37:1 (LXX 36:1)). A rebuke happens by word; the one who does not submit to the yoke of the teacher is chastised by the anger of God—and chastisement is more grievous than rebuke.
translator_notes: Copy-text PG 12 (Migne) Rufinus Latin via Archive PDF pdftotext; no first-edition GCS.
True OET: no ANF; do not copy Trigg FOTC / Prinzivalli SC / Perrone 2015.
After tip b07a2fd2; Psalms Rufinus Homilia I in Ps 37 CLOSEOUT.
orientation: Origen is beginning his homily on Psalm 37, quoting the psalmist's opening plea to the Lord and distinguishing verbal rebuke from the harsher chastisement of God's anger.

title: The heavy burden and Christ's invitation
english: "Like a heavy burden they have been made heavy upon me" (Psalm 37:4 (LXX 36:4)). "Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened" (Matthew 11:28). Glory to Christ. Amen.
